runs.brief: Fake-door landing page for a SolidWorks <-> Fusion feature-history translation bureau. Two equal direction doors, counted separately; disclosure plate before the card field at price type size; Stripe setup intent reservation.
runs.typeface: Archivo 400-800 variable, self-hosted latin subset rebuilt from upstream to carry U+2192 (the door arrow was falling back)
runs.plate: disclosure band, full-bleed signal fill, signal-ink type at --fs-price, kit bar in ink over the label, rails crossing at 22% ink
runs.notes: First Hallmark run for this project, so no rotation constraint applied. Grid chosen over a card-based theme because the exposed 12-column hairline rails read as drawing paper for a CAD audience; yellow over ultramarine to carry the McMaster tone reference and avoid default-AI blue. One deliberate departure from the theme, recorded rather than claimed as built: the display axis ships Archivo 700 in sentence case, not the theme's grotesk-heavy-lowercase, because 'SolidWorks' and 'Fusion' are trademarks that cannot be lowercased and the operator asked for the lighter McMaster heading voice. The plate was briefly diluted to an 18% signal wash to bring painted accent under the 5% accent-footprint cap, then reverted: grid.md:47 exempts the plate from that cap ('the plate is the one exception') and grid.md:82 bans wash and tint fills outside paper-2/paper-3, so the dilution was breaking the theme to satisfy a cap the plate is not under. Full-chroma signal is 48.4% of a 1280x800 viewport centred on the plate and that is the intended poster moment; signal-ink on signal measures 11.09:1, and .plate-text matches .price b at every width (20px to 768, 28px above).
